A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sortformer work. All 17 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–B, support comparison. Minor header crowding in v2 does not prevent recovering the table contents.

before.justification: v1 reports original Sortformer diarization experiments in Table I and multispeaker ASR experiments with WER and cpWER results in Table II.

after.justification: v2 reports revised original diarization results in Table I and retains the original multispeaker ASR results in Table II.

M1.justification: The Sortformer architecture, sort and hybrid losses, sorting procedures, speaker kernels, adapters and timestamp approximation remain unchanged. The revised NEST parameter count does not document an architectural modification.

E1.justification: Training corpora, tasks and evaluation coverage remain unchanged, including DIHARD3, CALLHOME-part2, CH109 and AMI-test. The reported reduction in simulated training hours changes data volume within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table I retains NeMo MSDD, EEND-EDA, WavLM-L+EEND-VC, EEND-GLA-Small/Large, AED-EEND and AED-EEND-EE. Table II retains the same Canary baseline and comparison configurations.

E3.justification: Section V-B reports that the second hybrid-loss setting uses approximately three fewer hours of LibriSpeech-based simulated data and more training epochs. Section V-A changes the reported NEST-L size from 108M to 115M parameters. Exact epoch counts remain unspecified; evaluation splits, metrics, collars and ASR settings are retained.

E4.justification: The evidence testing hybrid loss against PIL-only and sort-only training is revised through a second hybrid training setting and replacement of its Table I results. This does not isolate the effects of data amount and training duration. The postprocessing comparisons and Table II component ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seed information, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. The two hybrid training settings described in v2 are different configurations, not statistical replications.

E6.justification: Table I substantially revises the central hybrid-loss results. Four-speaker CALLHOME DER without/with postprocessing changes from 20.10/15.40 to 14.14/12.59, while DIHARD3 changes from 16.06/14.60 to 16.28/14.76. These are replacement results under changed training conditions. Four-speaker CALLHOME results without postprocessing also change for PIL, 21.94 to 18.80, and sort loss, 20.92 to 19.42. Table II is unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, loss formulations and derivations are unchanged. Appendices A–B retain the same permutation definitions and attention invariance/equivariance proofs, including equations 25–50.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about arrival-time sorting, hybrid-loss competitiveness, differentiable diarization–ASR integration and adapter-based multispeaker ASR.

C2.justification: The regularization explanation for hybrid loss, long-recording speaker-count limitations and interpretations of ASR supervision and token objectives remain unchanged. The added statement about mixed results between hybrid settings reports an observation without introducing a new mechanism or limitation.

D1.justification: v2 documents relative differences in simulated-data quantity and training duration between hybrid settings and revises the encoder parameter count. It does not provide exact epoch totals. Hardware, optimizer details, ASR training instructions and promised NeMo code/model availability remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and novelty positioning are unchanged. Reference text moves across pages without substantive bibliographic additions or removals.

P1.justification: Section IV changes its heading from 'Bridging Timestamps to Tokens' to 'Bridging Timestamps and Tokens.' Section V-B adds a short explanation of the hybrid training settings; the remaining narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 8 moves from the left to the right column on page 10 without changing its content, and subsequent text reflows. Table I changes header typography and its bottom rule; the CALLHOME speaker-count and collar headers become crowded and partly overlap.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency by partially explaining the revised hybrid training, but discusses two settings while Table I presents only one hybrid result pair without variant labels or exact epoch counts. Changed training prevents interpreting the updated scores as controlled performance gains, and crowded headers reduce readability. With the method, ASR evidence and appendices unchanged, these limited benefits and reporting drawbacks do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
